reason: E1 shows SRO destruction enhances ductility in CrCoNi, supporting the mechanism premise, but it does not address NbMoTaW, high-temperature performance, or irradiation resistance. E2 and E3 are irrelevant to SRO control or ductility in NbMoTaW, providing no support for the other key premises.
premises: Local destruction of SRO by dislocation glide creates softer zones and planar fault boundaries that enhance ductility
SRO and planar defects (SFs, TBs) can be controlled and are reversible under cyclic loading in HEAs
Controlling SRO and planar defects will promote dislocation slip and improve room-temperature ductility in NbMoTaW
High-temperature mechanical performance will not be compromised by SRO/defect control
Irradiation resistance will not be compromised by SRO/defect control
